newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close at new record.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close at new record.

text.p: French stocks reversed their early losses and rallied on Thursday to a second consecutive record close after the bourse shrugged off weakness on Wall Street and took its lead from rising European equities markets.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index rose 17.18 points, or 0.68 percent, to a closing record of 2,558.43 points, close to its all time intraday high of 2,558.60.
The CAC-40 February futures contract rose to 2,565 from 2,546.50 at Wednesday's close.
Volume was a heavy 8.9 billion francs.

"The bourse is ignoring bad news and has disconnected itself from Wall Street. It's trying to catch up relative to Frankfurt and London by finding new sources of inspiration in corporate results," a trader said.
He said strong resistance was seen at current levels.
* Elf Aquitaine rose 1.04 percent to 584 francs, extending its gains on a positive report from Merrill Lynch.

* Michelin rose 2.83 percent to 330.90 francs in brisk trading. Investors speculate a Goodyear-Sumitomo alliance will be to Bridgestone's detriment and to Michelin's advantage. They said Goodyear's good results were bullish for Michelin.
* Rhone-Poulenc slipped 0.49 percent after state holding CDR sold 4.6 percent of the chemicals group.
* Accor fell 1.2 percent to 740 francs. Fund managers said Societe Generale de Belgique was preparing to sell its holding in Accor which was nine percent last June.
* Suez rose 4.19 percent to 270.90 francs. Traders say it has benefitted from recent recommendations and favourable sentiment about its asset sales strategy.
* PSA Peugeot Citroen rebounded 4.36 percent after recent weakness. After the close it reported a 5.1 percent rise in 1996 turnover.
